title: the zeta variants, three families (FUNDAMENTALS-TRACK backward-fan band 2 over the S12 frontier)

concepts.name: the family factor: the term each index number carries

lesson.statement: the factor of a family is the term each index number carries: the minus family carries (1 minus i to the power minus s) and the plus family carries (1 plus i to the power minus s), and a family indexes the integers above one — all of them, the primes only, or the composites only

concepts.name: the index split: primes, composites, all — a partition of the integers above one

lesson.statement: the integers above one split into primes and composites and into nothing else: every integer above one is a prime or a composite, and is neither both; so a family over all of them is the product of the family over the primes and of the family over the composites, on both signs

concepts.name: the line partial: what a family holds up to the line end, a rational the store holds

lesson.statement: the families converge for the real part of s greater than one — the same half-plane where the store already holds the euler product; on my line the family is held as the partial product up to the line end 84, a rational the store can hold, and the limit over the whole infinite index past the line end is a step the store declares, not a number on my line

concepts.name: the term-removal: the product is multiplied by the reciprocal of the removed term

lesson.statement: the term-removal rule: when a term is removed from a product, the product is multiplied by the reciprocal of the removed term; when the prime p is removed from the minus family at s = 2, the multiplier is p squared over p squared minus one; the change of the output is determined exactly by the removed terms, and by nothing else

theorems.statement: where the index sets split, the product splits: for every family, the product over the integers above one is the product over the primes times the product over the composites — on my line the mechanism holds both sides as exact rationals, 85 over 168 both ways at s = 2

the minus family over all the numbers telescopes: (1 minus n to the power minus 2) is (n minus 1)(n plus 1) over n squared, so the partial product to height N is (N plus 1) over 2N — at my line end, height 84, that is 85 over 168, and every spot height on my line answers by the same rule

removing one prime from the minus family at s = 2 multiplies by p squared over p squared minus one: the change of the output is exactly the reciprocal of the removed term — for every prime on my line the store holds the multiplier as an exact rational
